```markdown
[Date]

Massachusetts Medicaid / MassHealth — Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — Hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914)**
**Member:** Skyler Grant
**Member ID:** W988301014
**Reference number:** POC-F65CAC945B-43805
**Date of denial notice:** August 3, 2026
**Plan:** Medicaid (Massachusetts)

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) that my surgeon, Dr. Duval, requested for me. The notice dated August 3, 2026 states that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, and refers generally to the plan's medical policy and clinical review criteria. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve this surgery.

**The specific criteria used to deny my request have not been shared with me.**

I want to be straightforward about one thing at the outset: I am not able to quote the plan's criteria back to the plan, because no policy title, section, or criteria language was given to me with the denial. The notice refers to medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not say what those criteria require — how long symptoms must last, how much conservative treatment is expected, what imaging findings count, or any threshold I would need to meet. I cannot show point by point that I meet a standard that has not been stated.

So I am asking for it in writing, as its own request: **please provide me with the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization for CPT 29914**, including the name of the policy or guideline, the specific criteria used, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination. I am sending a copy of this request to the Massachusetts Medicaid agency. If the plan applies criteria that my records do meet, I would like the chance to point that out; if the plan believes my records fall short of a specific requirement, I would like to know which requirement and by how much.

**What my records actually show**

In the meantime, here is what is documented in the prior authorization packet my surgeon submitted. I believe these facts support the surgery on their own.

- **My symptoms have gone on a long time and have gotten worse, not better.** I have had 14 months of progressive hip pain. It is not relieved by rest.
- **I did the non-surgical treatment first, and I completed it.** I finished 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, along with activity modification, from March 2, 2026 to June 22, 2026 — 18 visits. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **I tried medication and injection, and neither solved the problem.** I took NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief. I had a corticosteroid injection on May 4, 2026, which gave me only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging identifies a specific, structural, surgically treatable problem.** An MRI arthrogram of the hip on June 23, 2026 showed an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, with an alpha angle of 68 degrees. The joint space is preserved, Tonnis grade 0.
- **My exam matches the imaging.** Provocative testing is positive on the affected side, and my range of motion is limited by pain.
- **This affects my daily life.** I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and with pivoting. I cannot run and I cannot squat.
- **I am a reasonable surgical candidate.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I do not smoke.

Taken together: a documented structural lesion on imaging, physical exam findings that correspond to it, preserved joint space, more than a year of worsening symptoms, and a full course of physical therapy, medication, and injection that did not resolve the problem. My surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed and has submitted that documentation to the plan. I am not asking the plan to take my word for it — I am asking the plan to look at the packet Dr. Duval already sent.

**What I am asking for**

I ask that the plan overturn the denial and authorize the hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914) requested by Dr. Duval. If the plan maintains the denial, I ask that it tell me in writing the specific criterion my records did not satisfy, quoting the criterion itself, along with the clinical criteria I requested above and the reviewer's specialty. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with orthopedic surgery expertise.

I understand my appeal must be received by **January 30, 2027**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting this appeal to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, which is the address I am treating as authoritative. If I have sent this to the wrong place, please tell me right away so I can correct it within the time allowed. I understand that with Massachusetts Medicaid I may appeal through the state Medicaid agency or my managed-care plan, and that I may also request a state fair hearing, and I reserve my right to do so. If I have questions I can call the number on the back of my insurance card.

Please let me know if you need anything further from me or from Dr. Duval's office. I am happy to have additional records sent.

Thank you for reconsidering this decision.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Grant**
Member ID: W988301014
Reference number: POC-F65CAC945B-43805
[Street address]
[City, State, ZIP]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date of birth: [DOB]

**Enclosures:** [List what you send — e.g., physical therapy discharge note dated 2026-06-22; MRI arthrogram report dated 2026-06-23; office notes from Dr. Duval; copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-03]
**cc:** Massachusetts Medicaid agency — [address]; Duval, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
```

evidence.submission_route: Medicaid is run by your state. Appeal through your state Medicaid agency or your managed-care plan, and you can also ask for a state fair hearing. All of the details are on your denial letter. By phone: the number on the back of your insurance card Deadline: Often just 30 to 90 days — act quickly and check your letter -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
evidence.criteria_request: Most state Medicaid programs publish the rules for HOW a decision must be made but not the medical criteria for a specific surgery - those usually sit with your managed-care plan or its review vendor. Ask your plan in writing for 'the clinical criteria applied to my prior authorization', and copy your state Medicaid agency. Massachusetts, North Carolina and California are the exceptions - they publish real procedure criteria.
